package_info.why_malicious: The package is considered malicious because an attacker was able to hijack a previously popular repository namespace via a GitHub RepoJacking technique, allowing them to publish arbitrary code under a trusted package name. This enables supply chain attacks by serving malicious code to all downstream consumers who import the package by its original GitHub URL.

execution_context.file_location: main.go (or equivalent entrypoint in hijacked repo)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain via HTTP POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing sensitive environment variables and exfiltrating them to an external domain is a classic sign of malicious behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package code should not exfiltrate environment variables or perform network requests on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or error reporting libraries may send anonymized data, but never secrets or tokens.
key_indicators: Access to environment variables containing secrets
Execution at import-time (before user code runs)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads the user's private SSH key file and exfiltrates its contents to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reading private SSH keys and sending them to an external server is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never access or transmit private keys.

attack_chain.action: Attacker claims a previously retired GitHub namespace by creating a repo and then renaming the account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish code under a trusted package name.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious code to the hijacked repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now served to all downstream consumers.

attack_chain.action: Victims import the package via GitHub URL in Go/Swift/PHP projects.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on victim systems, exfiltrating secrets.

behavioral_signatures: Code in open-source packages that accesses environment variables or sensitive files at import-time
Network requests to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains during package initialization
file_indicators: Presence of code accessing environment variables or sensitive files in main.go or equivalent entrypoints
References to external domains in code comments or strings
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate package maintainer
POST requests containing environment variable values or file contents
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that have recently changed ownership or repository location, especially those with a history of high usage. Scan imported code for access to sensitive files or environment variables and for network requests to untrusted domains. Alert on any package that performs these actions at import-time or without user interaction.
